newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dry and cool weather hampers French beet recovery.
newsitem.headline: Dry and cool weather hampers French beet recovery.

text.p: The results of a fifth and last beet test conducted by French planters suggest dry weather and cool temperatures in September hampered sugar beet recovery, planters said.

The private test carried out on September 23 showed a "theoretical" sugar weight per hectare of 11.3 tonnes down from 11.7 tonnes in the same test last year and down six percent from the five-year average of 12 tonnes.
Sugar content, however, jumped to 18.7 percent from 16 percent last year and from the five-year average of 17.5 percent.
An analyst for the French beet planters federation (CGB) explained that a lack of sufficient rain in September and cool temperatures limited root growth but helped boost sugar content.
"It is now quite obvious that the beets will not make up ground lost earlier in the season," he said.
The latest results suggest the national beet sugar yield may fall to 9.5 tonnes per hectare this year from 9.8 tonnes last year, he added.
Beets in Normandy, Alsace and the Loiret areas had the best performance while crops in the Yonne and Oise regions suffered most from a prolonged drought in the spring.

A final official beet test carried out by the French sugar manufacturers on September 9 and released on September 13 -- that organisation's fourth -- showed sugar weight per hectare fell to 9.382 tonnes from 9.951 tonnes in the fourth test last year. This was a fall of 10.9 percent from the five-year average of 10.523 tonnes.
After the test, French sugar intervention board FIRS said it was maintaining its estimate of a 1996/97 beet sugar output of 3.9 million tonnes against 4.2 million in 1995/96.
Beet harvesting got under way last week in France, around the same time as last year, with at least one of the country's 45 processing factories starting operations.
But because the area is down this year there will be fewer beets to process. So refineries may stop operations three to four days earlier, planters said.
